National eco-boundaries

Source: R/ecoboundaries.R
ecoboundaries.Rd

Prepare boundaries based on Canadian national ecodistricts, -regions, -provinces, or -zones.

.ecoboundaries(
  type = NULL,
  destinationPath = tempdir(),
  studyArea = NULL,
  rasterToMatch = NULL
)

ecodistricts(
  destinationPath = tempdir(),
  studyArea = NULL,
  rasterToMatch = NULL
)

ecoregions(destinationPath = tempdir(), studyArea = NULL, rasterToMatch = NULL)

ecoprovinces(
  destinationPath = tempdir(),
  studyArea = NULL,
  rasterToMatch = NULL
)

ecozones(destinationPath = tempdir(), studyArea = NULL, rasterToMatch = NULL)

Arguments

type

character. The polygon type to use: Must be one of "ECODISTRICT", "ECOREGION", "ECOPROVINCE", or "ECOZONE".

destinationPath

character. Path to directory where data will be downloaded.

studyArea

(optional) sf object corresponding to the study area of interest.

rasterToMatch

(optional) template raster to use.

Examples

library(sf)
#> Linking to GEOS 3.12.1, GDAL 3.8.3, PROJ 9.3.1; sf_use_s2() is TRUE
library(sp)

## random study area in central Alberta
studyArea <- SpatialPoints(data.frame(lon = -115, lat = 55), proj4string = CRS("EPSG:4326")) |>
  st_as_sf() |>
  st_transform(paste("+proj=lcc +lat_1=49 +lat_2=77 +lat_0=0 +lon_0=-95",
                   "+x_0=0 +y_0=0 +units=m +no_defs +ellps=GRS80 +towgs84=0,0,0")) |>
  as_Spatial() |>
  SpaDES.tools::randomStudyArea(center = _, seed = 60, size = 1e10) |>
  st_as_sf()
